attacking an ancient and sacred custom. Tradition can preserve truth, but it can also preserve rebellion so efficiently that the descendants defend an error with greater enthusiasm than their fathers displayed when inventing it. Age does not make a practice biblical. It merely proves the practice has survived.
Elijah confronted the same divided allegiance on Mount Carmel. First Kings 18:21 records his question: “How long halt ye between two opinions? if the LORD be God, follow him: but if Baal, then follow him.” The issue was not whether the people could develop a religious program incorporating attractive features from both systems. Elijah demanded a decision concerning the true God. Jehovah and Baal were not complementary expressions of one acceptable religion. Their claims were opposed. The prophets of Baal could shout, leap, and mutilate themselves, but their enthusiasm could not produce an answer from heaven. Elijah's confrontation exposed the emptiness of their worship. Truth does not become stronger by borrowing a lie and offering it a seat beside the altar. When God has spoken, the believer's responsibility is to follow Him, not negotiate a religious partnership with the doctrines He condemns.
4. The Corrupted Sanctuary — When the Abomination Finally Moves Inside
The ultimate danger of tolerating idolatry beside the altar appears when the forbidden object eventually moves into the sanctuary itself. Second Kings 21:7 records concerning Manasseh, “And he set a graven image of the grove that he had made in the house.” The house was the LORD's temple, the place associated with His name among Israel. Yet Manasseh introduced an idolatrous image into that sacred setting. Consider how far the nation had departed from Deuteronomy 16. Moses had forbidden planting the grove beside God's altar. Generations later, a wicked king had established the associated image inside God's house. The boundary had not merely been approached; it had been crossed and trampled. Sin introduced as a neighbor seldom remains content with the property line. Give false worship a place beside the sanctuary, and sooner or later its advocates will begin explaining why the sanctuary itself should accommodate it.

Ezekiel 8 exposes additional abominations connected with the temple and the corruption of worship in Jerusalem. The prophet is shown an image of jealousy, idolatrous representations, secret practices, and men turning toward the east to worship the sun. These were not examples of pagan worship occurring in some distant country with no connection to Israel. The offenses had entered the sphere of the LORD's own house and the nation's religious leadership. Jeremiah 7:30 declares, “For the children of Judah have done evil in my sight, saith the LORD: they have set their abominations in the house which is called by my name, to pollute it.” The text is unmistakable. God's name upon a building did not make the abominations acceptable. Their presence polluted the place. A sanctuary does not possess the magical ability to convert wickedness into holiness. Sometimes the very presence of wickedness inside a sacred place makes the offense greater because the people are openly defying the God they profess to honor.
This is why Scripture repeatedly condemns attempts to substitute religious activity for obedience. Saul discovered that lesson when he preserved what God had commanded to be destroyed and attempted to justify his conduct through sacrificial intentions. First Samuel 15:22 declares, “Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.” Nadab and Abihu likewise offered strange fire before the LORD, contrary to His command, and suffered judgment in Leviticus 10. The principle is not that all religious innovation carries identical consequences in every dispensation. The principle is that human sincerity cannot overrule divine instruction. Hi Nthabiseng,

I saw your post, and I just want to say: please don’t be so hard on yourself. The pain and frustration you’re feeling right now are completely valid. Looking at a payslip that barely stretches, and realizing you’re turning 40 without a pension, is a terrifying wake-up call. But I need you to hear this: this is not your fault, and you are definitely not alone.

Here are a few things you need to know:

1. You are in the majority, not the minority
According to recent stats, only about 6% to 10% of South Africans are actually on track to retire comfortably. Millions of working people, many with degrees, have zero retirement savings. Our economy, the cost of living, and the high unemployment rate have made it almost impossible for ordinary people to save. You are fighting a systemic battle, not a personal one.

2. Don't let your payslip invalidate your degree
Was going to university worth it? Absolutely. Your transcript doesn't just represent a piece of paper; it proves your resilience, your discipline, and your ability to finish what you start. A degree gives you options, critical thinking skills, and the potential to grow your income. Even if the financial reward feels delayed right now, that qualification is your ticket to a better future. Don’t let the current economic climate convince you otherwise.

3. You still have time. Here is what you can do right now:

· Start small: You don’t need thousands of rands to start. Open a Retirement Annuity (RA). Start with R500 or R1,000 a month if you can afford it. The key is consistency.
· Use the tax man: RA contributions are tax-deductible (up to 27.5% of your income). This means SARS essentially subsidizes a portion of your saving.
· Increase it every year: Commit to increasing your monthly RA contribution by 10% (or whatever you can afford) every time you get a raise.
· Be careful with the Two-Pot system: If you have an employer fund, do everything you can to leave the savings pot alone. Let compound interest work for you.
· Talk to HR: Check if your employer offers a group retirement fund, as the fees are usually much lower than individual RAs.

Nthabiseng, 40 is not the end. You are still in your prime earning years. The fact that you are looking at your payslip and asking these hard questions means you are ready to take control. Give yourself some grace. You are doing the best you can with the cards you've been dealt.

You've got this. 💪❤️

text:
Jordan’s Wizards years are more interesting when you stop asking them to look like his Bulls years.

The separation was harder to create. The recovery took longer. The player who once seemed capable of imposing his will on an entire season had to negotiate with his body.

But watch the footwork. The shoulder fake. The patience to get a defender leaning before rising for the jumper.

Washington made the craftsmanship easier to appreciate because the athleticism could no longer overwhelm the conversation.

In his final season, Jordan played all 82 games and averaged 20 points, turning 40 along the way.

The Wizards missed the playoffs. This wasn’t another chapter of championship dominance, and pretending otherwise adds nothing to his legacy.

What it offered was a different perspective on it.

Even with so much of his physical advantage gone, there was still an NBA scorer underneath: balance, timing, touch and an extraordinary understanding of how to create a shot.

The flights made him famous.

The Wizards years offered a reminder of how much basketball he knew after landing.

text:
🚨 I’ve been crunching the numbers on Restore Britain, using the Electoral Calculus and Find Out Now MRP poll (6,699 GB adults, fieldwork 25 September to 2 October 2026).

MRP (multilevel regression and post-stratification) takes a large national poll and models it down to seat level using each constituency’s demographics.

Support for Restore is very limited in Wales and especially Scotland, so I’ve focused on England.

The top ten English seats for Restore (ties included) are identical to the GB list:

Great Yarmouth (32%)

Easington (19%)

Blyth and Ashington (17%)

Ashfield (16%)

Joint 5th on 15%: Barnsley South; Basildon and Billericay; Durham North; Hull East; Rawmarsh and Conisbrough.

Joint 10th on 14%: Barnsley North; Blackpool South; Bradford South; Havant; Normanton and Hemsworth; Pontefract, Castleford and Knottingley; Rotherham; Stoke-on-Trent Central; Wolverhampton South East.

At the other end, Harpenden and Berkhamsted is the only English seat on 2%.

Because 10th place falls within an 18-way tie on 3%, the bottom ten runs to 19 seats: Bicester and Woodstock; Cambridgeshire South; Chelmsford; Cheltenham; Didcot and Wantage; Dorset West; Esher and Walton; Guildford; Harrogate and Knaresborough; Maidenhead; Richmond Park; St Neots and Mid Cambridgeshire; Sussex Mid; Sutton and Cheam; Tunbridge Wells; Wimbledon; Winchester; Woking.

I then tested all 543 English seats, rather than only the extremes, so any conclusions rest on the full pattern. I used Open Innovations’ constituency dataset, which converts official statistics (ONS, Census 2021, the MHCLG deprivation index and others) to the 2024 boundaries.

I compared Restore support with deprivation, estimated 2016 Leave vote, higher education entry, country of birth, age, child poverty, the claimant rate and life expectancy.

The pattern broadly fits the familiar “left behind” geography of Brexit and Reform, with two complications: the strength of deprivation, and the absence of an age effect.

Brexit is the strongest single predictor. Estimated Leave vote correlates with Restore support at ρ = 0.68 and alone explains about 40% of the variation between seats. The top 18 seats have a median Leave vote of 69%; the bottom 19, 45%.

Deprivation comes close behind (ρ = 0.49), and life expectancy (ρ = −0.55) and child poverty (ρ = 0.40) point the same way. The top seats have a median deprivation score of 33.2 against 9.7 in the bottom seats, life expectancy of 78.5 years against 83.2, and child poverty of 33.6% against 16.9%. Average support rises steadily from 6.5% in the least deprived fifth of seats to 10.9% in the most deprived.

Crucially, deprivation keeps a clear independent effect once Leave vote is controlled for. Education, which looks strong on its own (ρ = −0.49), drops to zero. The education gap seems to run through Brexit identity, while deprivation adds something beyond it.

Birthplace matters less than you might expect. The share of UK-born residents is only weakly linked to support (ρ = 0.22). Within each level of deprivation the more UK-born seats do run higher, peaking at 12.5% in seats that are both deprived and overwhelmingly UK-born. Deprived, diverse urban seats are generally low (Birmingham Ladywood 7%, Tottenham 7%, Hackney South 5%), but not uniformly: Derby South (13%), Smethwick and Coventry East (both 12%) sit above the English median.

Age shows no relationship. The share of over-65s is unrelated to support (ρ = 0.03), which cuts against an “older voters” story, at least at seat level.

Region and local politics leave much unexplained. The North East averages 11.3%, while London, the South West and the South East average around 7%. Even combined, these factors explain only about 55% of the variation. The biggest underperformers include Lib Dem strongholds: North Cornwall, Torbay, North Devon, Sutton and Cheam, Chelmsford and North Norfolk. The biggest overperformers are North East former mining seats (Easington, Blyth and Ashington, North Durham), along with the Reform-held Basildon and Billericay and Ashfield.

Some caveats.

Because MRP estimates are built from demographic predictors, these correlations partly reflect the modeller’s assumptions rather than independent evidence. The seats that defy their demographics are the more telling part. The poll also assumes don’t knows vote as they did in July 2024, when Restore didn’t stand, which may slightly understate its support.

Great Yarmouth’s 32% likely reflects Rupert Lowe’s personal vote as the sitting MP, so I left it out of the regressions. These are seat-level patterns and can’t tell us which individuals back Restore. Lastly, the education measure is young people’s HE entry rate, a proxy for adult degree attainment.

If deprivation really does carry weight of its own, beyond Brexit identity, then one plausible way to blunt Restore Britain’s appeal is to reduce the conditions it feeds on.

This analysis can’t prove cause and effect, but it fits wider research: Thiemo Fetzer’s study of austerity, published in the American Economic Review in 2019, linked welfare cuts after 2010 to rising UKIP support and, by extension, the Leave vote.

Essentially, the places where Restore polls strongest are places with shorter lives, higher child poverty and fewer young people going to university.

Tackling those things won’t win over committed ideologues, but it could shrink the pool of people for whom a party like Restore seems to offer answers.

Tactical voting under FPTP may be the main way to avoid right-wing populists getting a bigger foothold in parliament, but arguably the most important thing Andy Burnham’s Government can do to reduce the rise of the far right in the UK, and especially England, is what it’s always been: reduce concentrated poverty and deprivation.

Restore Britain’s strongest seats are former mining communities in the North East and South Yorkshire, along with neglected coastal and post-industrial towns, places where people die years earlier and a third of children grow up in poverty.

Those voters have heard decades of promises about “levelling up” and seen little change.

A government that delivers visible improvements in jobs, health, housing and high streets in those places would do more to drain support from the far right than any amount of messaging.

Without that, every by-election and local contest gives Reform and Restore another chance to tell people that nobody else is listening.

text:
Elon Musk might be the most powerful Austrian economist on the planet.

The crashes of 1929 and 2008 ruined millions of people. Same culprit both times: the State and its central bank.

And while politicians keep playing with the money printer, Elon is making their power obsolete. Not through a coup. Through value creation.

Masterclass.

First, what is the Austrian School?

An economic tradition born in Vienna in 1871 with Carl Menger, then carried forward by Ludwig von Mises and Friedrich Hayek (Nobel Prize, 1974). Its core ideas are simple.

Value is subjective. It comes from individual choices, not decrees.

Money is not an invention of the State. It emerges from the market, from a real and scarce good. Mises showed this as early as 1912.

Prices are information. Hayek explained in 1945 that no central planner can gather the knowledge scattered across millions of people. The price system does it on its own.

The entrepreneur is the engine of the economy: the one who allocates capital where it creates the most value.

And in 1976, Hayek went even further with The Denationalisation of Money: he proposed stripping governments of their monopoly on issuing money and letting private currencies compete.

Now reread what Elon is saying.

Fiat money becomes obsolete. Energy is the true currency. Governments can print money, but they can't print energy. Capital will flow to those who best allocate energy to produce more goods and services.

Money backed by a scarce physical asset, out of politicians' reach, and entrepreneurs allocating resources instead of planners.

That's Mises and Hayek, 21st-century edition, with rockets and robots.

So why are Austrians so wary of the State? Because their theory explains the great crises. And they all share the same signature.

Here's the mechanism: the central bank holds interest rates artificially low. Credit becomes too cheap. Entrepreneurs and households launch projects that would never be profitable at the real price of money. That creates a boom. Then rates rise, the projects collapse, and you get the crash.

Start with 1929.

The Fed is created in 1913. Through the 1920s, it lets credit explode. In 1927, it even cuts rates, partly to prop up the British pound. Easy money fuels a monstrous stock bubble: people buy stocks on margin with 10% down.

In October 1929, the bubble bursts.

And that's when the State turns a recession into a catastrophe. The Fed lets the money supply shrink by roughly a third between 1929 and 1933, and thousands of banks fail. In 1930, Congress passes the Smoot-Hawley tariff, raising duties on thousands of products and triggering a global trade war. Hoover pressures businesses not to cut wages, preventing the labor market from adjusting. Roosevelt follows with price controls and government-organized cartels.

Result: 25% unemployment and a crisis that lasts an entire decade.

Now fast forward to 2008.

After the dot-com bubble bursts, Alan Greenspan's Fed takes rates from 6.5% in 2000 down to 1% in 2003, and keeps them there for a year.

Meanwhile, the State pushes homeownership for everyone. Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, two quasi-public giants with an implicit government guarantee, buy up mountains of mortgages. The federal FHA accepts 3% down payments. Banks know they're "too big to fail": if it breaks, taxpayers will pay.

Free credit + public guarantee + moral hazard = the biggest housing bubble in history.

Then the Fed raises rates to 5.25% by 2006. Borrowers can't pay. Lehman Brothers collapses in September 2008.

And the State's response? Exactly what caused the problem in the first place: zero rates, a $700 billion bank bailout, then years of massive money printing. We treated a debt crisis with more debt, and an easy-money crisis with more easy money.

Two crises, one pattern: the State manipulates the price of money, creates a bubble, then makes citizens pay when it pops.

Now look at what Elon is doing.

For 50 years, space was a government monopoly. After the Shuttle was retired in 2011, the US paid Russia to fly its astronauts. Today SpaceX does it, at a fraction of the cost, and launches most of everything that reaches orbit on the planet.

Communications infrastructure was a sovereign domain. Starlink now connects entire regions, including war zones, where governments failed to build anything.

Energy was the business of public monopolies. Tesla installs giant batteries that stabilize national power grids.

And now he's going after the last monopoly, the most sacred of all: money.

He didn't seize power. He didn't overthrow anyone. He just built things that work better than what the State offered. And people, companies, and even governments chose to use them.

That's the real Austrian revolution. You don't destroy the State by force. You make it progressively irrelevant by creating more value than it does.

Not by seizing power. By outbuilding it.

text:
Elon says money will become obsolete and energy will be the true currency.

Half my timeline understood: "there won't be any currency anymore."

It's the exact opposite.

There will always be a currency. What's going to die is fiat money. And with it, the power of the people who print it.

Quick masterclass on why.

First, what is money?

Money isn't wealth. It's a tool. It has three functions: unit of account (measuring value), medium of exchange (avoiding barter), and store of value (carrying today's work into tomorrow).

At its core, money is a database. It records who produced what, and who has the right to consume what. It's a system for allocating human labor.

And good money has one non-negotiable property: you can't create it out of thin air. Otherwise, it lies.

For centuries, money was backed by something real: gold. Every banknote was a claim on a weight of metal. You couldn't print more than what you had in the vault.

Then we dismantled it, piece by piece.

In 1914, World War I. Countries suspend gold convertibility to finance the war on credit.

In 1933, Roosevelt bans Americans from owning gold and devalues the dollar right after.

In 1944, Bretton Woods. The dollar becomes convertible to gold at $35 an ounce, and every other currency gets pegged to the dollar.

On August 15, 1971, Nixon "temporarily" suspends the dollar's convertibility to gold. That "temporary" measure has now lasted 55 years.

In 1973, exchange rates float. Not a single major currency in the world is backed by anything physical anymore.

Since 1971, the dollar has lost nearly 90% of its purchasing power. US federal debt has grown almost 100x. Housing prices have decoupled from wages. That's not a coincidence. It's the direct consequence of money with no physical limit.

Now, central banks.

A central bank does two things: it sets the price of money (interest rates) and it creates money. Two massive levers, in the hands of a handful of people nobody elected.

When they keep rates too low for too long, they create bubbles, keep zombie companies alive, and push everyone into debt.

When they print, they dilute your savings. The Fed's balance sheet went from roughly $900 billion in 2007 to nearly $9 trillion in 2022. The US money supply grew about 40% between 2020 and 2022. Result: 9.1% inflation in the US in June 2022, 10.6% in the eurozone in October 2022.

Inflation is a tax nobody voted for. And it doesn't hit everyone equally: those closest to money creation (the state, banks, asset holders) get the new money first. Workers and savers get it last, after prices have already gone up.

Now let's reason from first principles.

If AI and robotics produce most goods and services, human labor is no longer the limiting factor of the economy.

So a currency whose job is to allocate human labor no longer has a purpose.

What stays scarce?

Energy.

Every physical good is matter transformed with energy. Every AI is computation, meaning electricity. With enough energy, you extract, you recycle, you manufacture, you reason.

The natural unit of account of a robotic economy isn't the dollar. It's the kilowatt-hour.

And this is where it gets beautiful: energy-backed money is tied to a real, measurable asset governed by thermodynamics. As Elon puts it, governments can print money, but they can't print energy.

No more inflation manufactured by bureaucrats playing with the printing press. We go back to a standard. But this time, not a metal sitting in a vault: the very input of all production.

My prediction: within the next ten years, the fiat monetary system will break. And with it, the grip that politicians and legacy bankers have on money.

Elon is designing the new global economic order. Not a communist system: private property stays central. But capital will flow to those who best allocate energy to create more goods and services. A meritocracy of physics.

That's what will bring us abundance.

Money isn't disappearing. It's becoming honest again.

Russian dachas as Trojan horses. A Trojan horse in the White House. Georgia was taken over by a Kremlin Trojan horse.

The Kremlin has established a network of recreational properties in the Baltic Sea region that could serve as staging grounds for sabotage and hybrid operations against the West. Authorities in Sweden, Norway, and Lithuania are already scrutinizing hundreds of homes owned by Russians—properties located alarmingly close to key military bases and critical infrastructure.
Security officials are increasingly vocal about the threat posed by the real estate market. Hundreds of holiday homes across the Baltic and Scandinavian regions have fallen into the hands of individuals with ties to Moscow. Experts and politicians explicitly warn that these properties could function as "Trojan horses."

"In the Baltic states, there is a genuine concern that Russia could use these properties as a kind of Trojan horse," notes Eitvydas Bajarūnas, Lithuania’s former ambassador to London.

An oligarch’s wife’s estate near a strategic naval base

The most alarming case concerns Sweden. Authorities in Stockholm have identified a luxury estate—situated right at the entrance to the Muskö naval base, one of the country’s most sensitive defense facilities—as a "critical threat."  The seven-room villa belongs to Tatyana Sazonova, the wife of Stanislav Aleshchenko—a Russian oligarch with close ties to Vladimir Putin.

Swedish Minister of Defence Pål Jonson has announced that the state will take over the property.

"It is the only location in the area that is not accessible to the Swedish Armed Forces, which creates a critical gap in the defense of the naval base. The property is currently owned by a Russian citizen, posing a threat to national security."

Regaining control over this site is essential, not least due to the growing risk of drone attacks.

In Norway and Lithuania

A similar pattern is emerging in other NATO countries. In Norway, holiday homes owned by individuals linked to the Kremlin offer a direct view of the strategic Bardufoss airbase, where assets such as F-35 fighter jets are stationed.

In Lithuania, Russian citizens have acquired properties in the immediate vicinity of North Atlantic Alliance bases. In response, Vilnius has already introduced legislation prohibiting Russians from purchasing land or buildings near sensitive facilities.

Drone threats and sabotage in Europe

These unassuming vacation homes could serve as observation posts, secure hideouts for sabotage groups, or launch sites for attack drones targeting Western installations.  The use of these properties is part of a broad-ranging hybrid warfare campaign waged by Moscow. Its objective—involving acts of sabotage across Europe, including attacks on industrial facilities in countries such as the United Kingdom and Poland—is to paralyze Western military support for Ukraine.

US Ambassador to Türkiye and special presidential envoy Tom Barrack said on October 20 that American ground intervention against Yemen’s Ansar-allah movement would likely be fruitless, acknowledging that Saudi Arabia faces a “very difficult position.” Speaking at the Global Security Forum in Doha, Qatar, Barrack said President Donald Trump supports Riyadh and will provide logistical assistance but does not intend to commit US forces to a ground battle. “These kinetic reactions have never worked. It doesn’t work. It’s probably not likely that it’s going to work,” he said.

Barrack argued that regional governments should take greater responsibility for their own security rather than depend on Washington. Referring to Ansar-allah in Yemen, Hezb-ollah in Lebanon and armed factions in Iraq, he said such groups would lose their rationale if states addressed the political and security conditions that sustain them. He also questioned the effectiveness of past US regime-change efforts and urged regional governments to develop their own alliances and pursue dialogue.

His remarks come amid renewed fighting between Yemen’s Ansar-allah movement and forces backed by Saudi Arabia. The United States conducted more than 1,000 airstrikes against Yemen between March and April 2025, seeking to halt attacks on Red Sea shipping. On May 6, 2025, Washington announced an Oman-mediated agreement to stop bombing the movement, although the deal did not require an end to attacks on Israel. With hostilities escalating again in 2026, Saudi Arabia has sought greater support from international partners. Barrack’s comments signal Washington’s reluctance to undertake another direct ground campaign, even as it continues to offer Riyadh logistical backing.

text:
I warned you, now it's happening

— Marc Elias 

Democracy Docket
Founder 

The start of early voting is normally a time for civic celebration. For Aaron Reitz, the U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Texas, it was an opportunity to make a threat.
 
Standing beside a Bible and a framed photograph of Donald Trump, Reitz recorded a video promising there would be no “crooked local election administrators.” They “have a duty to prevent illegal voting,” he said, “and I’m here to make sure they do their job.”
 
Then he got to the point: “If you violate federal election law, I will hunt you down and prosecute you.”
 
Reitz did not cite a single example of election malfeasance. Nor did he offer any evidence of fraud.
 
But deterring bad actors wasn’t his real goal. His message was aimed squarely at the county clerks and poll workers who run our elections. And, of course, he was playing to an audience of one in the White House.
 
He is not alone.
 
On Friday, Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter sent a letter warning California election officials that they could face criminal liability if they count ballots as state law requires. At issue are mail ballots sent to 20,000 voters the DOJ claims are “likely” noncitizens.
 
The letter made clear that anyone who “knowingly tabulate[s] ballots cast by individuals identified by federal agencies as noncitizens” risks becoming an aider and abettor to a federal crime.
 
Note that McCotter is not describing ballots confirmed to be from noncitizens, only ballots the federal government thinks likely are. Under this theory, any list of voters the Trump administration wants excluded becomes grounds for threatening criminal charges against the officials who count their ballots.
 
To sharpen the point, Bill Essayli, the First Assistant U.S. Attorney in Los Angeles, amplified the warning. He cited the federal aiding-and-abetting statute that, under the Trump DOJ’s theory, would make election officials guilty of a felony.
 
As if choreographed for maximum effect, Trump then shared the letter on Truth Social and added his own threat aimed at California’s election officials: “They will all go to jail for a long period of time.”

text:
At the height of the dot-com mania, a young investor stood up at Berkshire Hathaway's annual meeting and asked Warren Buffett a question.

If Kleiner Perkins, the most famous venture firm in Silicon Valley, offered him a stake in a $1 billion internet fund, would he take it?

Buffett said no.

It was 1999. Tech stocks only went up.

Over the next months, that answer looked like a mistake. Barron's put Buffett on its cover under the headline "What's Wrong, Warren?" Berkshire's stock fell roughly in half from its 1998 high.

Buffett agreed the internet would change the world. That wasn't his problem. His problem was how people were making money from it: early investors sell to the next round, who sell to the next round, "at twice the price."

In the end, he said, the companies have to "succeed as businesses." Most wouldn't.

In March 2000, the Nasdaq peaked. Over the next two and a half years it fell 78%. https://t.co/1VYvgsQxiJ, Webvan and hundreds of others went to zero.

Berkshire's stock bottomed almost the same week the Nasdaq peaked.

In the video below, Buffett explains why Berkshire will never hand its money to anyone else: "If we're gonna lose your money, we're gonna lose it ourselves and come back and look you in the eye and tell you how we lost it."

The young investor was Mohnish Pabrai. He took the answer to heart. Years later, he paid $650,100 at a charity auction for lunch with Buffett.

Same bubble. Same internet. Same question.

Would you have taken the fund?

Beyond Crypto: Exploring Bitget’s New CFD Assets

As a crypto trader, I’ve learned that not every market gives a clear opportunity all the time. Sometimes, the market moves sideways, and forcing trades just because you want to make a profit can do more harm than good.

That’s one reason I like seeing Bitget expand its CFD offering with 8 new trading assets across base metals, energy, and global indices. It gives traders more markets to explore instead of relying entirely on crypto.

Why I’m Looking at the Taiwan Index

One asset that caught my attention is the Taiwan RIC Index ($TWRICC).

With AI and semiconductor technology continuing to attract global attention, Taiwan is a market worth watching because of its important role in the global chip industry. Rather than focusing only on individual tech stocks, the Taiwan Index offers another way to follow movements in that market through CFDs.

Of course, the AI narrative alone isn’t a reason to enter a trade. Price action, key levels, and market confirmation still matter.

More Markets, More Options

Beyond indices, Bitget’s new CFD assets include opportunities in metals and energy. These markets have their own drivers, from industrial demand and supply conditions to global economic developments.

I find this interesting because crypto isn’t always moving in the same direction as traditional markets. Having access to different asset classes creates more flexibility when looking for potential setups.

One Account, Different Markets

Another thing worth highlighting is that Bitget allows traders to access CFDs alongside stocks and crypto under one account. That makes it easier to explore different markets without constantly switching between platforms.

For me, diversification isn’t about trading everything at once. It’s about having more options, understanding what drives each market, and choosing the setups that actually make sense.

Bitget’s latest CFD expansion is a welcome addition. I’ll be keeping an eye on the new listings, especially $TWRICC, while letting the charts guide my decisions rather than chasing every market move.

Sometimes, the next opportunity might be outside crypto.

Jensen Huang's message is interesting: telecom networks won't just carry data. They could increasingly carry AI intelligence.
Think about what telecom operators already own — cell sites, regional infrastructure, connectivity and access to millions of users.
NVIDIA wants to help turn parts of that network into distributed AI computing infrastructure.
That could create another market for its accelerated computing and networking platforms.
But there's a second investment angle here.
For telecom operators, AI-RAN could eventually offer new revenue opportunities beyond traditional connectivity, alongside more efficient network operations.
T-Mobile's live-network demonstration is encouraging, while other operators are progressing through trials and planned deployments.
My take: I see this as another example of NVIDIA expanding its role across the AI infrastructure stack.
The opportunity is significant, but commercial adoption and operator economics still need to be proven.
AI infrastructure may increasingly extend beyond the data centre and into the networks connecting everything.

Strengthen my faith when I am weary, and grant me the divine wisdom to achieve my goals while honoring You. I place my life, my health, my deepest longings, and my wildest dreams entirely into Your blessed hands. Guide every activity I undertake, help me make choices that reflect Your grace, and let my actions always exalt Your Holy Name. Forgive me for the times I have failed You, Lord, and transform my heart daily so that I may be a reflection of Your love to everyone I meet. Keep my lamp burning bright and my soul anchored in service, so that when You return, You find me watching, ready, and worthy to sit at Your divine table.
Waking up to this new morning is a profound blessing. You have poured out Your infinite grace upon us, asking for nothing in return but our faith. Though we are forever in debt to Your mercy, we offer You our hearts and souls in absolute trust.
On this midweek morning, I lift up our nation and the entire world to You. Lord, watch over our country and guide our leaders with wisdom, integrity, and compassion. Wrap Your almighty, healing hands around the sick who are holding onto hope, and provide warmth and shelter to the homeless who need comfort. May God grant us all a healthy mind and a peaceful heart today. Happy Wednesday, everyone. Rest in the beautiful assurance that God always has your back.

text:
This argument confuses reform with negation and offers speculation in place of historical evidence.

Ambedkar did not simply invent a religion to oppose Hinduism. He consciously reinterpreted Buddhist Dhamma through The Buddha and His Dhamma, grounding it in morality, reason, social equality and human dignity. Navayana is a distinct modern interpretation of Buddhism, but that does not make it an artificial religion.

His 22 vows rejected Hindu deities and practices because he believed they perpetuated caste hierarchy. Rejecting a system of oppression is not the same as building an identity with nothing positive of its own. Liberty, equality, fraternity and the annihilation of caste were constructive goals, not merely acts of negation.

The claim that Ambedkarites are destined for a “second round of conversion” is speculation, not evidence. And invoking Sharjeel Imam to imply that Ambedkarites are a recruitment ground for Islam requires actual proof, not insinuation.

The real question is not whether Ambedkar rejected Hinduism, but whether caste discrimination could be overcome while remaining within its social hierarchy. Criticise his conclusions if you wish-but historical claims require evidence, not conspiracy theories disguised as intellectual analysis.

text:
AN HUMBLE ATTEMPT TO PROMOTE EXPLICIT AGREEMENT AND VISIBLE UNION OF GOD’S PEOPLE - IN EXTRAORDINARY PRAYER - FOR THE REVIVAL OF RELIGION AND THE ADVANCEMENT OF CHRIST’S KINGDOM ON EARTH
By Jonathan Edwards (1703 – 1758)

Every Wednesday, DV

Continuing...

PART 1: SECTION IV

A memorial from several ministers in Scotland, to their brethren in different places, for continuing a Concert for Prayer, first entered into in the year 1744.

Whereas it was the chief scope of this concert to promote more abundant application to a duty that is perpetually binding, prayer that our Lord’s kingdom may come, joined with praises: and it contained some circumstantial expedients, apprehended to be very subservient to that design, relating to stated times for such exercises, so far as this would not interfere with other duties; particularly a part of Saturday evening and sabbath morning, every week; and more solemnly of some one of the first days of each of the four great divisions of the year, that is, of each quarter; as the first Tuesday, or first convenient day after; 316 and the concert, as to this circumstance, was extended only to two years; it being intended, that before these expired, persons engaged in the concert should reciprocally communicate their sentiments and inclinations, as to the prolonging of the time, with or without alteration, as to the circumstance mentioned: and it was intended by the first promoters, that others at a distance should propose such circumstantial amendments or improvements, as they should find proper: it is hereby earnestly entreated, that such would communicate their sentiments accordingly, now that the time first proposed is near expiring.

II. To induce those already engaged to adhere, and others to accede to this concert; it seems of importance to observe, that declarations of concurrence, the communicating and spreading of which are so evidently useful, are to be understood in such a latitude, as to keep at the greatest distance from entangling men’s minds: not as binding men to set apart any stated days from secular affairs, or even to fix on any part of such and such precise days, whether it be convenient or not: not as absolute promises in any respect; but as friendly, harmonious resolutions, with liberty to alter circumstances as shall be found expedient. On account of all which latitude, and that the circumstantial part extends only to a few years, it is apprehended, the concert cannot be liable to the objections against periodical religious times of human appointment.

III. It is also humbly offered to the consideration of ministers, and others furnished with gifts for the most public instructions, whether it might not be of great use, by the blessing of God, if short and nervous scriptural persuasives and directions to the duty in view, were composed and published, (either by particular authors, or several joining together; which last way might sometimes have peculiar advantages,) and that from time to time, without top great intervals; the better to keep alive on men’s minds a just sense of the obligations to a duty so important in itself, and in which many may be in danger to faint and turn remiss, without such repeated incitements: and whether it would not also be of great use, if ministers would be pleased to preach frequently on the importance and necessity of prayer for the coming of our Lord’s kingdom; particularly near the quarterly days, or on these days themselves, where there is public worship at that time.

IV. They who have found it incumbent on them to publish this Memorial at this time, having peculiar advantages for spreading it, do entreat that the desire of concurrence and assistance contained in it, may by no means be understood as restricted to any particular denomination or party, or to those who are of such or such opinions about any former instances of remarkable religious concern; but to be extended to all, who shall vouchsafe any attention to this paper, and have at heart the interest of vital Christianity, and the power of godliness; and who, however differing about other things, are convinced of the importance of fervent prayer, to promote that common interest, and of scripture persuasives to promote such prayer.

V. As the first printed account of this concert was not a proposal of it, as a thing then to begin, but a narration of it, as a design already set on foot, which had been brought about with much harmony, by means of private letters; so the farther continuance, and, it is hoped, the farther spreading of it, seems in a promising way of being promoted by the same means; as importunate desires of renewing the concert have been transmitted already from a very distant corner abroad, where the regard to it has of late increased: but notwithstanding what may be done by private letters, it is humbly expected, that a memorial spread in this manner, may, by God’s blessing, further promote the good ends in view; as it may be usefully referred to in letters, and may reach where they will not.

VI. Whereas in a valuable letter, from the corner just now mentioned, as a place where a regard to the concert has lately increased, it is proposed, that it should be continued for seven years, or at least for a much longer time than what was specified in the first agreement; those concerned in this Memorial, who would wish rather to receive and spread directions and proposals on this head, than to be the first authors of any, apprehend no inconvenience, for their part, in agreeing to the seven years, with the latitude above described, which reserves liberty to make such circumstantial alterations, as may be hereafter found expedient: on the contrary it seems of importance, that the labour of spreading a concert, which has already extended to so distant parts, and may, it is hoped, extend further, may not need to be renewed sooner, at least much sooner; as it is uncertain but that may endanger the dropping of it; and it seems probable, there will be less zeal in spreading it, if the time proposed for its continuance be too inconsiderable. Meantime, declarations of concurrence for a less number of years may greatly promote the good ends in view; though it seems very expedient, that it should exceed what was first agreed on; seeing it is found on trial, that that time, instead of being too long, was much too short.

VII. If any person who formerly agreed to this concert, should now discontinue it; would it not look too like that fainting in prayer, against which we are so expressly warned in Scripture? And would not this be the more unsuitable at this time, in any within the British dominions, when they have the united calls of such public chastisements and deliverances, 317 to more concern than ever about public reformation, and consequently about that which is the source of all thorough reformation, the regenerating and sanctifying influence of the Almighty Spirit of God: August 26, 1746.

N. B. The minister in Boston afore-mentioned to whom most of the copies of this Memorial were sent, who, I suppose, has had later and more full intelligence than I have had concerning the proposal, in a letter, The motions seem to come from above, and to be wonderfully spreading in Scotland, England, Wales, Ireland, and in North America.
***********************

314 As may be seen by comparing ver. 3. with Isa. lx. 14.—ver. 4. with Isa. lxv. 20.22. and Isa. xxxiii. 24.—ver. 6, 7, & with Ezek. xxxvii. 2, 11, 12. 21.—ver. 7. with Isa. xliii. 5, 6. and xlix. 12. and lix. 19.—ver. 12, 13. with Hos. ii. 21, 22. and Ezek. xxxiv. 22-39. ver. & 12, 13. with Ezek. xxxvi. 28-30.—ver. 13. with Zeph. iii. 20. and Isa. xix. 24.—ver. 19, with Isa. lxi. 3.and Jer. xxxi. 12, 13, 14.
315 Zech. viii. 21.
316 The meaning is, the first Tuesdays of February, May, August, and November, or the first convenient days after these.
317 Alluding, probably, to the rebellion in 1743, and the defeat of the rebels..-W.

Alphabet’s stake in Anthropic expands

The value of Alphabet’s stake in the artificial intelligence start-up Anthropic has soared to around $US124 billion ($178 billion), making it one of the most lucrative bets in the company’s history.The Google parent disclosed in a filing on Thursday (Friday AEST) that the value of its investments in unidentified private companies totalled roughly $US124.3 billion as of June 30. The filing noted that this value is “primarily” driven by one investment, which is a reference to Alphabet’s stake in Anthropic, according to a person familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified because the information is not public. The company said it recorded about $US77 billion in unrealised gains from its private investments in the second quarter, without providing further details in the filing. Google has emerged as one of Anthropic’s biggest backers over the past several years. The technology giant first invested $US3 billion in the start-up starting in 2023. Earlier this year, it agreed to invest as much as $US40 billion more, consisting of $US10 billion upfront and a potential $US30 billion in additional funding tied to operational and financial milestones through 2030.Alphabet’s filing on Thursday showed the remaining commitment has fallen to $US20 billion as of June 30 from $US30 billion at the end of the first quarter, suggesting that Google invested another $US10 billion in the start-up last quarter. Australian Mining

Global Commodity Rankings

Australia holds some of the world's largest reserves and is a leading producer of several key minerals.

#1 Producer: Iron Ore, Bauxite, Lithium, Rutile, and Zircon.

#1 Reserves: Iron Ore, Gold, Lead, Nickel, Rutile, Uranium, and Zinc.

#2 Producer: Gold, Alumina, and Manganese.

Key Mining Hubs & Major Projects

Western Australia: The nation's "engine room," producing 98% of Australia's iron ore and 60% of its gold. Major sites include the Pilbara (iron ore) and the Super Pit in Kalgoorlie (gold).

Queensland: A global leader in metallurgical coal (Bowen Basin) and silver/lead production (Cannington mine).

South Australia: Home to Olympic Dam, which contains the world's largest single uranium deposit and significant copper and gold reserves.

Major Players

The sector is dominated by several multinational giants and significant domestic players:

BHP: Often ranked as Australia's most valuable company; major interests in iron ore, copper, and coal.

Rio Tinto: A world leader in iron ore (Pilbara) and aluminum.

Fortescue (FMG): Primarily focused on iron ore and rapidly expanding into green energy.

Hancock Prospecting: Australia's largest private mining company, led by Gina Rinehart, the nation's wealthiest person.

South32: Spun out of BHP; manages a diversified portfolio including manganese, silver, and nickel.

2026 Trends & Developments

Critical Minerals Push: The government has introduced a $23 billion package to support domestic processing and manufacturing of critical minerals to reduce global reliance on single-country supply chains.

Uranium Rally: Prices exceeding US$100/lb have sparked renewed interest in Australian prospects like the Kalkaroo project.

M&A Activity: Major merger talks continue between giants like Rio Tinto and Glencore as they seek to consolidate copper exposure for the EV market.

Workforce Challenges: The Minerals Council of Australia is currently calling for migration reforms to address a significant "skills crunch" in the sector.

The “Our Hong Kong Foundation–Dah Sing Bank Greater Bay Area Industry Development Index 2026” (the “Index”) will be jointly launched on 22 October by Our Hong Kong Foundation (“OHKF”) and Dah Sing Bank, Limited (“Dah Sing Bank”). 
 
 With the GBA advancing high-quality development and industrial upgrading, businesses across the region are increasingly turning to modern professional services. Intellectual property (IP) -- covering intangible assets such as technological innovation, brand equity, and creative assets – is emerging as a vital enabler of enterprise growth. Furthermore, Testing, inspection, and Certification (TIC) services, supported by broader mutual recognition of standards, offer a practical pathway to accelerate market expansion and enhance competitiveness across global supply chains. 
 
 OHKF’s research team tracks the performance of 11 cities in the GBA across six key industries — Financial Services, Innovation & Technology, Trade & Logistics, Manufacturing, Construction & Real Estate, and Culture, Sports & Tourism. The Index analyses the development strategies and potential of GBA enterprises under the two focused themes — IP and TIC services — providing valuable references for policymakers, businesses, and research institutions to help them capitalise on future opportunities.

The Index Press Conference and Panel Session (the “Conference”) will feature a panel session to address the subject of “Navigating the Seas – IP and TIC application of GBA Enterprises”. This panel session invites distinguished industry leaders to delve into how IP and TIC services can empower businesses to strengthen their competitive edge within global supply chains and successfully navigate an ever-changing international trade landscape.

Alphabet’s stake in Anthropic expands

The value of Alphabet’s stake in the artificial intelligence start-up Anthropic has soared to around $US124 billion ($178 billion), making it one of the most lucrative bets in the company’s history.The Google parent disclosed in a filing on Thursday (Friday AEST) that the value of its investments in unidentified private companies totalled roughly $US124.3 billion as of June 30. The filing noted that this value is “primarily” driven by one investment, which is a reference to Alphabet’s stake in Anthropic, according to a person familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified because the information is not public. The company said it recorded about $US77 billion in unrealised gains from its private investments in the second quarter, without providing further details in the filing. Google has emerged as one of Anthropic’s biggest backers over the past several years. The technology giant first invested $US3 billion in the start-up starting in 2023. Earlier this year, it agreed to invest as much as $US40 billion more, consisting of $US10 billion upfront and a potential $US30 billion in additional funding tied to operational and financial milestones through 2030.Alphabet’s filing on Thursday showed the remaining commitment has fallen to $US20 billion as of June 30 from $US30 billion at the end of the first quarter, suggesting that Google invested another $US10 billion in the start-up last quarter. Mining/Energy/Resources/Biz

Rio Tinto dodges merger bullet

Rio Tinto has dodged two 'bullets' due to Glencore's rejection of a merger proposal: a possible BHP takeover bid and a dangerous acquisition. BHP looked closely at whether to bid for Rio Tinto if the latter announced a merger with Glencore. The two companies would make excellent merger partners; amongst others things, their staff and senior people have similar cultures, they are co-operating on future Australian iron ore projects and they are copper joint venture partners in Chile and the US. Meanwhile, there are significance cultural differences between Rio Tinto and Glencore; there is little doubt that Rio Tinto's CEO Simon Trott would have had doubts about a merger once he understood these cultural differences. (RMS)

News/Snapshot

Australian Mining

Global Commodity Rankings

Australia holds some of the world's largest reserves and is a leading producer of several key minerals.

#1 Producer: Iron Ore, Bauxite, Lithium, Rutile, and Zircon.

#1 Reserves: Iron Ore, Gold, Lead, Nickel, Rutile, Uranium, and Zinc.

#2 Producer: Gold, Alumina, and Manganese.

Key Mining Hubs & Major Projects

Western Australia: The nation's "engine room," producing 98% of Australia's iron ore and 60% of its gold. Major sites include the Pilbara (iron ore) and the Super Pit in Kalgoorlie (gold).

Queensland: A global leader in metallurgical coal (Bowen Basin) and silver/lead production (Cannington mine).

South Australia: Home to Olympic Dam, which contains the world's largest single uranium deposit and significant copper and gold reserves.

Major Players

The sector is dominated by several multinational giants and significant domestic players:

BHP: Often ranked as Australia's most valuable company; major interests in iron ore, copper, and coal.

Rio Tinto: A world leader in iron ore (Pilbara) and aluminum.

Fortescue (FMG): Primarily focused on iron ore and rapidly expanding into green energy.

Hancock Prospecting: Australia's largest private mining company, led by Gina Rinehart, the nation's wealthiest person.

South32: Spun out of BHP; manages a diversified portfolio including manganese, silver, and nickel.

2026 Trends & Developments

Critical Minerals Push: The government has introduced a $23 billion package to support domestic processing and manufacturing of critical minerals to reduce global reliance on single-country supply chains.

Uranium Rally: Prices exceeding US$100/lb have sparked renewed interest in Australian prospects like the Kalkaroo project.

M&A Activity: Major merger talks continue between giants like Rio Tinto and Glencore as they seek to consolidate copper exposure for the EV market.

Workforce Challenges: The Minerals Council of Australia is currently calling for migration reforms to address a significant "skills crunch" in the sector.

Australian Mining

Global Commodity Rankings

Australia holds some of the world's largest reserves and is a leading producer of several key minerals.

#1 Producer: Iron Ore, Bauxite, Lithium, Rutile, and Zircon.

#1 Reserves: Iron Ore, Gold, Lead, Nickel, Rutile, Uranium, and Zinc.

#2 Producer: Gold, Alumina, and Manganese.

Key Mining Hubs & Major Projects

Western Australia: The nation's "engine room," producing 98% of Australia's iron ore and 60% of its gold. Major sites include the Pilbara (iron ore) and the Super Pit in Kalgoorlie (gold).

Queensland: A global leader in metallurgical coal (Bowen Basin) and silver/lead production (Cannington mine).

South Australia: Home to Olympic Dam, which contains the world's largest single uranium deposit and significant copper and gold reserves.

Major Players

The sector is dominated by several multinational giants and significant domestic players:

BHP: Often ranked as Australia's most valuable company; major interests in iron ore, copper, and coal.

Rio Tinto: A world leader in iron ore (Pilbara) and aluminum.

Fortescue (FMG): Primarily focused on iron ore and rapidly expanding into green energy.

Hancock Prospecting: Australia's largest private mining company, led by Gina Rinehart, the nation's wealthiest person.

South32: Spun out of BHP; manages a diversified portfolio including manganese, silver, and nickel.

UNANIMOUS NINTH CIRCUIT PANEL BLOCKS CALIFORNIA'S 'NO VIGILANTES ACT'

A three-judge panel of the Ninth Circuit has blocked California's "No Vigilantes Act," which required non-uniformed federal law enforcement officers operating in the state to visibly display identification while carrying out their duties.

Federal agents who violated the requirement could have faced state criminal prosecution.

The court pointed to the Constitution's Supremacy Clause, which establishes federal law as the "supreme Law of the Land," and the principle that states cannot directly regulate federal government operations.

The panel also invoked precedent stretching back to the landmark 1819 Supreme Court decision McCulloch v. Maryland.

California argued that its law was permissible because it did not "substantially burden" federal law enforcement.

The Ninth Circuit rejected that argument, concluding that a state cannot directly regulate federal conduct regardless of the degree to which the law interferes with federal operations.

Writing for Fox News Opinion, @HvonSpakovsky says the ruling offers California officials a lesson in constitutional supremacy.

text:
Today, I honoured an invitation from United Port Services Private Limited for a working visit to Hyderabad, Telangana, and Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh, India, to learn from its agricultural investment model and explore opportunities to transform 35,000 acres in the Bura Irrigation Scheme into a large-scale rice production hub.

The visit provided an opportunity to understand how private-sector investment, modern agricultural practices and large-scale irrigation infrastructure can be leveraged to increase agricultural productivity, strengthen food security and reduce dependence on food imports.

We visited the Polavaram Irrigation Project, a major multipurpose water infrastructure investment in India, with a reported gross reservoir storage capacity of approximately 5.51 billion cubic metres (BCM). The project is designed to bring an additional 720,000 acres under irrigation while stabilising water supplies for a further 2.35 million acres across the Godavari and Krishna delta regions, supporting a combined agricultural area of approximately 3.07 million acres. It also incorporates a 960 MW hydroelectric power plant and facilitates the transfer of Godavari River water to the Krishna basin. The project demonstrates how integrated investments in water storage, irrigation and hydropower can enhance agricultural productivity, strengthen water security and drive economic development.

India, with a population of over 1.4 billion projected to reach approximately 1.7 billion by 2067, recognises the importance of strategic investments in irrigation and agricultural modernisation to meet growing food demand. Its experience offers valuable lessons for Kenya as we pursue our national food security objectives.

The proposed investment in the Bura Irrigation Scheme presents a significant opportunity to apply these lessons. With an estimated yield of 30 bags per acre, the planned 35,000-acre development has the potential to produce approximately 1.05 million bags of rice, equivalent to 78,750 metric tonnes per production cycle, assuming each bag weighs 75 kilogrammes.

Such an investment would contribute significantly to increasing domestic rice production, reducing the food import bill, creating employment opportunities, improving farmers' incomes and stimulating economic activity along the agricultural value chain. With appropriate infrastructure, a reliable water supply, modern farming technologies and efficient market linkages, Bura can become a major contributor to Kenya's rice production.

As the Government implements the National Irrigation Sector Investment Plan (NISIP), which targets the expansion of irrigation by one million acres over ten years, partnerships with the private sector will be critical to mobilising the capital, technology and expertise required to accelerate irrigation development.

🌿 WISDOM FOR 2027: NOT EVERY SWEET THING IS GOOD FOR YOU!

Sugarcane is sweet, but nobody swallows it.

There are lessons in this simple saying that every Nigerian, especially our youths, should understand as we approach the 2027 general elections.

Sometimes, what looks attractive today may become a problem tomorrow. We must learn to look beyond temporary benefits and consider the future we want for ourselves and our children.

🇳🇬 WHY WE MUST BE CAREFUL WITH MONEY DURING ELECTIONS

As the 2027 elections approach, Nigerians must be careful not to allow financial inducements to determine their political choices. This warning applies to APC and every other political party.

If politicians or their supporters offer money, rice, food items, or other gifts in exchange for votes, remember that your vote is worth more than a temporary gift.

💰 Money can finish in one day, but the consequences of a political decision can last for years.

🍚 A bag of rice cannot solve the problems of unemployment, insecurity, poor electricity, rising living costs, or inadequate healthcare.

🗳️ Your PVC represents your opportunity to participate in choosing leaders. Do not surrender that opportunity for a payment that cannot guarantee a better future.

⚠️ OUR PLAN AS RESPONSIBLE CITIZENS

1. Educate our people.
Let us teach our friends, family members, and community members to examine candidates' records, policies, and promises before making their decisions.

2. Question every political promise.
Ask politicians what they intend to do about jobs, education, healthcare, security, electricity, and the cost of living.

3. Be careful of election-season generosity.
When politicians suddenly begin distributing money and gifts, ask yourself whether the gesture comes with expectations about your vote. Do not assume every gift is a vote-buying attempt, but remain alert to any condition attached to it.

4. Refuse to sell your future.
Make your political decision freely. Do not allow anyone to threaten, pressure, or deceive you into voting against your conscience.

5. Promote peaceful participation.
We can disagree politically without insulting one another, spreading unverified allegations, or engaging in violence.

6. Demand accountability after the election.
Our responsibility does not end when we vote. We must continue asking elected officials to fulfil their promises.

🔥 MY MESSAGE TO NIGERIAN YOUTHS

My brothers and sisters, let us remember that Nigeria belongs to all of us.

No political party owns your future. No politician should determine your worth by the amount of money they offer you.

Whether the offer comes from APC, another political party, or an independent political actor, make sure your decision reflects your conscience and your understanding of the issues.

Do not exchange tomorrow's opportunities for today's temporary benefits.

Remember the wisdom of the sugarcane: something can be sweet at first and still require careful consideration.

In 2027, let us prioritise issue-based campaigns, credible information, peaceful elections, and accountability.

Our future is bigger than election-season gifts. Our votes deserve careful consideration. Our democracy deserves our participation.

✍️ Esomuchi (Esobest)
Mayor of the People

Documented cases exist of people of color (including Black individuals) being listed as White on booking records or related databases, often due to self-reporting, officer perception, administrative categories, or data-entry errors. Race recording in U.S. criminal justice systems is imperfect—Hispanic/Latino is typically an ethnicity (not a race), many systems default or group categories in ways that favor “White,” and visual appearance does not always match listed race because of mixed ancestry or lighting/photo quality. 
Portland 2020 protest bookings
A Village Portland report documented multiple people of color arrested during protests who were booked as White or “unknown.” One clear example is Chris Wise, a biracial Black man (father African American) and volunteer protest medic. He was arrested for disorderly conduct and interfering with a police officer; his booking information listed “Race: White.” He posted the mugshot with the caption “I told them I was black.” The reporter spoke with 17 people who reported similar misidentification. Police said race is based on what the person offers or perceived race; the sheriff’s office said it copies from arrest documents. Analysts noted error rates exceeding typical data-entry mistakes. 
Sex offender registries and other records
Analyses of public registries (especially Texas DPS) have highlighted numerous entries listed as “White, Non-Hispanic” (or similar) for people whose photos appear Black, Hispanic, or otherwise non-White. Independent reviews and social-media threads (including from accounts examining the full Texas database) have flagged many such discrepancies—far more non-White appearances listed as White than the reverse in the datasets examined. Illinois State Police has also noted records where an African American photo is paired with a White race code, recommending checks against FBI criminal history. One common collage of Texas registry photos illustrates the pattern of varied appearances under White/Non-Hispanic labels.

Turkey’s reported breakthrough in Libya is more than a Mediterranean dispute. It highlights Ankara’s expanding strategic network across the Mediterranean, Red Sea and Indian Ocean.

🇱🇾 Mediterranean: On 20 October 2026, Libya’s eastern-based House of Representatives reportedly voted unanimously to approve the controversial 2019 Turkey–Libya maritime memorandum, marking a significant shift in eastern Libya’s relationship with Ankara.

A Major Political Reversal

The approval represents a dramatic change for an administration long associated with military commander Khalifa Haftar, whose political camp had previously opposed the agreement and taken a hostile stance towards Turkey. The vote signals a potential rapprochement between Benghazi and Ankara, with wider implications for diplomatic relations, investment, energy exploration and regional security.

🇸🇴 Indian Ocean : Turkey’s 10-year defence and economic cooperation framework with Somalia supports the development of its navy, while separate agreements open opportunities for Turkish offshore oil and gas exploration.

🇩🇯 Red Sea gateway: Turkey’s defence cooperation with Djibouti strengthens its regional relationships near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, one of the world’s most important shipping routes.

🇸🇩 Sudan’s Red Sea coast: The proposed redevelopment of Suakin Island reflects Turkey’s interest in strategic port infrastructure, although the project’s implementation and military implications remain uncertain.

What Does This Mean for #Greece, #Cyprus and #Israel?

Turkey’s partnerships extend its strategic reach across vital shipping routes, energy interests and security networks. For Greece and Cyprus, this adds another dimension to their maritime disputes with Ankara.

Israel has also entered the Somaliland equation. In December 2025, Israel became the first country to formally re-recognise Somaliland as an independent state, adding a new dimension to diplomacy and security in the Horn of Africa and the Gulf of Aden.

Somaliland: A Strategic Opportunity for Athens and Nicosia?

With its own institutions, relative stability and the strategically located port of Berbera, Somaliland presents an important question for European and Eastern Mediterranean diplomacy.

Greece and Cyprus could expand diplomatic, economic and maritime-security cooperation with Somaliland and examine whether formal recognition would serve their long-term interests.

Recognising Somaliland and deepening maritime cooperation could offer Greece and Cyprus a strategic response mirroring Turkey’s move in Libya, opening a new geopolitical front in the Gulf of Aden and Red Sea while strengthening their regional influence and maritime partnerships.

If Turkey is expanding its strategic partnerships from the Mediterranean to the Indian Ocean, why should Greece and Cyprus not reconsider their approach to Somaliland and explore maritime cooperation around the Gulf of Aden and Bab el-Mandeb? 

Such a move could help counterbalance Ankara’s regional influence and serve as a strategic response to the Turkey–Libya maritime agreement, which Athens argues undermines the maritime rights of Greek islands, particularly Crete.

The competition is not simply about maritime boundaries. It is also about diplomatic relationships, strategic access and influence along the world’s most important sea routes.

What are the new heaven and the new earth?
Answer
In Revelation 21:1, John sees something spectacular: “Then I saw ‘a new heaven and a new earth,’ for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away.” This new earth and new heaven are sometimes referred to as the “eternal state.” As seen in Revelation chapters 21—22, the new earth will be the eternal dwelling place of believers in Jesus Christ. Scripture gives us a few details of the new heaven and new earth.

The current heaven and earth have long been subject to God’s curse because of mankind’s sin. All creation “has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth” (Romans 8:22) as it awaits the fulfillment of God’s plan and “the children of God to be revealed” (verse 19). Heaven and earth will pass away (Mark 13:31), and they will be replaced by the new heaven and the new earth. At that time, the Lord, seated on His throne, says, “I am making everything new!” (Revelation 21:5). In the new creation, sin will be totally eradicated, and “there shall be no more curse” (Revelation 22:3, NKJV).

The new heaven and new earth are also mentioned in Isaiah 65:17; 66:22; and 2 Peter 3:13. Peter says that the new heaven and new earth will be “where righteousness dwells.” Isaiah says that “the former things will not be remembered, nor will they come to mind.” Things will be completely new, and the old order of things, with the accompanying sorrow and tragedy, will be gone.

The new earth will be free from sin, evil, sickness, suffering, and death. It will be earth as God originally intended it to be, prior to the curse of sin. It will be Eden restored.

A major feature of the new earth will be the New Jerusalem. John calls it “the Holy City . . . coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride beautifully dressed for her husband” (Revelation 21:2). This glorious city, with its streets of gold and pearly gates, is situated on a new, glorious earth. The tree of life will be there (Revelation 22:2). This city represents the final state of redeemed mankind, forever in fellowship with God: “God’s dwelling place is now among the people, and he will dwell with them. They will be his people, and God himself will be with them and be their God. . . . His servants will serve him. They will see his face” (Revelation 21:3; 22:3–4).

In the new heaven and new earth, Scripture says, there are seven things notable for their absence—seven things that are “no more”:
• no more sea (Revelation 21:1)
• no more death (Revelation 21:4)
• no more mourning (Revelation 21:4)
• no more weeping (Revelation 21:4)
• no more pain (Revelation 21:4)
• no more curse (Revelation 22:3)
• no more night (Revelation 22:5)

The creation of the new heaven and new earth brings the promise that God “will wipe every tear from their eyes” (Revelation 21:4). This event comes after the tribulation, after the Lord’s second coming, after the millennial kingdom, after the final rebellion, after the final judgment of Satan, and after the great white throne judgment. The brief description of the new heaven and new earth is the last glimpse into eternity that the Bible gives.

Digital Reading Habits for Cozy Mystery Fans

A good mystery has a way of following you around. One chapter becomes three while the coffee brews, or you sneak in a few pages while waiting at the veterinarian's office. Digital reading habits make those small pockets of time feel like a private visit to a favorite small town, complete with suspicious glances, friendly neighbors, and perhaps one very observant dog.

For cozy mystery readers, the appeal of reading digitally is not simply convenience. It is the ability to keep a comforting story close at hand. Still, a phone full of alerts is not always the peaceful reading nook we had in mind. A few thoughtful choices can help digital reading feel less like screen time and more like settling into a good book.

## Why Digital Reading Habits Matter

Cozy mysteries invite readers to pay attention. A stray comment from a shopkeeper, a muddy paw print, or a detail about an old Florida building may matter later. When reading is constantly interrupted, it becomes harder to gather those pleasant little clues and enjoy the slow unfurling of the puzzle.

That does not mean every reader needs a perfect routine. Some people happily read on a phone during lunch, while others prefer an e-reader with no distractions at all. The best device is the one you will use comfortably, but it helps to be honest about what pulls your attention away from the story.

Digital reading can also make it easier to read more often. Your current book does not get left on the kitchen table when it lives on the device already in your bag. Adjustable text, built-in dictionaries, bookmarks, and notes can make reading more welcoming for people whose eyes tire easily or who enjoy checking an unfamiliar word without losing their place.

## Choose a Device That Suits Your Reading Life

An e-reader is often the calmest choice for long stretches of fiction. Its screen is designed for reading, and many models allow readers to adjust font size, line spacing, margins, and warmth of the page color. That matters when a pleasant evening with a mystery turns into a very late night because the culprit is finally within reach.

A tablet offers color, easy browsing, and room for illustrations, but it can tempt readers toward email, games, and social media. A phone is wonderfully portable, especially for short waits and travel, yet its smaller screen may feel cramped during a long reading session. There is no wrong answer. A phone can be perfect for a chapter in line at the pharmacy, while an e-reader may be better for a rainy afternoon on the porch.

Try not to judge your reading preferences by someone else's. If larger type helps you relax, use larger type. If a dark background feels easier at night, choose it. The point is not to make reading look a certain way. The point is to stay comfortably inside the story.

### Make the Page Easy on Your Eyes

Tiny print and bright screens can turn even the cleverest whodunit into a squinting contest. Increase the font until it feels pleasant, not merely tolerable. Give the text enough spacing that your eyes can move easily from line to line.

At night, dim the screen and consider a warmer display setting. In daylight, raise the brightness only as much as needed. If your eyes feel dry or sore, take a brief break, look across the room, and give your eyes a chance to refocus. A mystery will wait patiently for five minutes. The suspects are not going anywhere.

## Protect the Quiet Around the Story

The biggest challenge in digital reading is usually not the book. It is everything else living on the same device. One notification can lead to a message, then a news headline, then a half hour disappears like a missing piece of evidence.

Before reading, silence alerts or use a focus setting. Even twenty undisturbed minutes can feel surprisingly generous. If you read on a phone or tablet, consider moving the reading app to the first screen and placing more distracting apps somewhere less convenient. This is not about scolding yourself for checking your phone. It is about making the choice to return to the book easier.

A small ritual helps, too. Put on a kettle, find a comfortable chair, or let the dog settle beside you before opening the book. Repeating a simple cue tells your brain that this is reading time. It can be especially helpful after a busy day, when the mind is still racing through chores, appointments, and unanswered questions.

## Read in Small, Satisfying Windows

Many readers assume they need a free evening to make real progress in a book. Cozy mysteries are particularly friendly to shorter sessions because each chapter often offers a fresh conversation, a new clue, or a delightful complication. Ten minutes can be enough to revisit familiar characters and move the case along.

Look for natural reading windows rather than trying to force a grand schedule. The first few minutes after breakfast, a lunch break, a waiting room, and the quiet before bed can all become reliable reading moments. If bedtime reading makes you sleepy in the nicest possible way, set the device aside when your eyelids begin to win. There is charm in saving a few chapters for tomorrow.

Some readers enjoy setting a daily page or time goal. Others find goals turn a pleasure into homework. It depends on your personality. A gentler promise, such as reading one chapter whenever you can, often keeps the habit warm and sustainable.

## Use Digital Tools Without Turning Reading Into Homework

Bookmarks are useful when life interrupts, and notes can be a treat for readers who love tracking clues. Mark a passage when a character says something that feels slightly off, or jot down a question about an alibi. Later, it is satisfying to see whether your instincts were right.

But not every mystery needs a case file. Cozy fiction should leave room for surprise, laughter, and the pleasure of being led down a charmingly crooked path. If notes make you feel like you are preparing for an exam, skip them. A simple bookmark is enough.

Samples can also be helpful when choosing your next read. Read a few pages and listen for the voice. Do the characters feel like people you would enjoy spending time with? Does the setting give you a sense of place? In the Doc and Daisy Mysteries, for instance, Daisy's canine point of view adds a warm snout, sharp observations, and a little extra mischief to the investigation. The right digital book is the one that makes you want to read one more page before you put the device down.

### Keep Your Place Across Devices

If you switch between a phone, tablet, and e-reader, make sure your reading app is set to sync your progress. Nothing spoils a good reveal quite like accidentally jumping backward fifty pages or, worse, landing ahead of the chapter you had reached.

When syncing is unreliable, use a bookmark before changing devices and give the app a moment to update. It is a small habit, but it prevents the sort of confusion usually reserved for a mystery's most tangled family tree.

## Let Reading Be a Comfort, Not Another Task

Digital tools are helpful when they support your reading life, not when they make it feel managed to the last minute. You do not need a color-coded tracker, a perfect streak, or a towering annual total to be a real reader. You need a story that catches your interest and enough quiet to hear it unfold.

Keep a book ready for the odd little gaps in the day. Make the page comfortable. Protect a few minutes from interruptions. Then let yourself enjoy the pleasures of a well-placed clue, a quirky town, and a detective who knows that sometimes the smallest detail - perhaps noticed by a very good dog - is the one that matters most.
