Trump touted the deal at his North Carolina rally this week: 𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘋𝘦𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘵𝘮𝘦𝘯𝘵 𝘰𝘧 𝘞𝘢𝘳 𝘸𝘪𝘭𝘭 𝘣𝘦 𝘪𝘯𝘷𝘦𝘴𝘵𝘪𝘯𝘨 $1.5 𝘣𝘪𝘭𝘭𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘵𝘰 𝘱𝘳𝘰𝘥𝘶𝘤𝘦 𝘤𝘶𝘵𝘵𝘪𝘯𝘨-𝘦𝘥𝘨𝘦 𝘴𝘦𝘮𝘪𝘤𝘰𝘯𝘥𝘶𝘤𝘵𝘰𝘳 𝘤𝘩𝘪𝘱𝘴 𝘳𝘪𝘨𝘩𝘵 𝘩𝘦𝘳𝘦 𝘪𝘯 𝘕𝘰𝘳𝘵𝘩 𝘊𝘢𝘳𝘰𝘭𝘪𝘯𝘢 𝘢𝘭𝘴𝘰. 𝘐𝘵’𝘴 𝘣𝘳𝘦𝘢𝘬𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘯𝘦𝘸𝘴.

The chips in question aren't the kind that run a laptop. Wolfspeed makes 𝐬𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐜𝐨𝐧 𝐜𝐚𝐫𝐛𝐢𝐝𝐞 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐠𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐮𝐦 𝐧𝐢𝐭𝐫𝐢𝐝𝐞 semiconductors — the hardened components used in drones, radar systems, missile defense, and electronic warfare, exactly the hardware America can't afford to source from a rival. Wolfspeed's largest U.S. footprint runs through North Carolina, where the administration wants that production anchored for good.

The timing matters. Wolfspeed filed for bankruptcy protection barely a year ago. Instead of watching a strategic chip supplier go under or get bought out from overseas, the Pentagon is betting taxpayer-backed capital on keeping the production — and the jobs — on American soil.

Every dollar of defense-chip capacity built here is a dollar China and Taiwan's supply chain no longer control.

text:
The Mind Illuminated - A Complete Meditation Guide Integrating Buddhist Wisdom and Brain Science.pdf

CULADASA (JOHN YATES, PH.D.) AND MATTHEW IMMERGUT, PH.D. WITH JEREMY GRAVES

THE MIND ILLUMINATED 

A COMPLETE MEDITATION GUIDE INTEGRATING BUDDHIST WISDOM AND BRAIN SCIENCE (Cont.)

pg. 438-443

STAGE EIGHT

Mental Pliancy and Pacifying the Senses

The goal of Stage Eight is complete pacification of the senses and the full arising of meditative joy. Simply continue to practice, using skills that are now completely effortless. Effortlessly sustained exclusive attention will produce mental and physical pliancy, pleasure, and joy.

Stage Eight: The meditator leads, and the elephant obediently follows. The mind has been tamed. The monkey and the rabbit are gone: scattering of attention and dullness are no longer a threat.

• The elephant has become completely white as the hindrances of Ill-will and Agitation Due to Worry and Remorse are replaced by the blisses of physical and mental pliancy.

• There is no flame, because meditation is effortless. 

PRACTICE GOALS FOR STAGE EIGHT

You begin Stage Eight as an adept practitioner. You can consistently pacify the discriminating mind and enter a state of mental pliancy. In other words, you have effortlessly stable attention and powerful mindfulness. Each sit, it can take a while to reach effortlessness, and sometimes you’ll stay at Stage Six or Seven the whole time. But you should be able to reach mental pliancy fairly regularly and remain there for the rest of the sit.

Much of the practice at this Stage simply involves exercising your newly compliant mind’s abilities to explore.

Think of your mind as an unknown territory where no one else has been, and no one but you can go. You alone are responsible for how you proceed, and how you use your skills and develop your mind.

You have two goals for this Stage. As an adept meditator—with a highly compliant mind due to a complete pacification in Stage Seven—your first goal is to exercise this mind, explore its nature, and discover and develop its inherent abilities. Think of your mind as an unknown territory where no one else has been, and no one but you can go. A spiritual teacher can point you in certain directions, make suggestions based on their own experience, and offer valuable methods developed by other meditators in the past. After all, one human mind isn’t so different from another. But it’s your own needs and interests that will determine how you actually proceed. Follow wherever they take you. I promise, you will go places and do things with your mind that are pointless to describe or discuss with anyone who hasn’t made this journey for themself.

The second major goal is complete pacification of the senses, which produces physical pliancy and fully developed meditative joy. Since both pacification of the senses and meditative joy result from the same unification process, we treat them as two parts of a single goal. To pacify the senses, you will exclude all sense objects from attention while sustaining metacognitive awareness. To cultivate meditative joy, you don’t need to do anything different or special, just keep practicing. It will arise naturally once the sensory minds grow quiet and the mind as a whole becomes sufficiently unified.

You’ve mastered Stage Eight when your eyes perceive only an inner light, your ears perceive only an inner sound, your body is suffused with pleasure and comfort, and your mental state is one of intense joy. 

EXERCISING THE NEWLY COMPLIANT MIND

Your first goal is to exercise the skills you’ve already mastered in order to explore the nature of the mind and fully develop its inherent abilities. Mental pliancy gives you effortlessly stable attention and sustained, powerful mindfulness, particularly in the form of metacognitive introspective awareness. The practices in the next section will help you experiment with attention.

text:
What did a woman’s work in an Egyptian temple look like? This painted figure offers a glimpse, with a rattle held upright in her hand.

Dating to about 1250–1200 BCE, this fragment of a tomb painting from Deir el-Medina shows a woman holding a sistrum: a rattle that women often played in temple ceremonies. Her image survives in paint applied to plaster over mud. The damaged inscription includes a reference to Amun, leading the Walters Art Museum to suggest that she may have belonged to his temple staff. The instrument makes her religious activity visible, even though the surviving words cannot tell us her complete story. Music could be part of the work of worship.

That is a small but vivid glimpse of a woman’s religious role. Also, an excellent assignment for anyone whose family has complained that they make too much noise. 😹🎶

Photo: The Walters Art Museum, 32.9, CC0; square detail crop.

ちなみに、「君の名」（５３）の大庭秀雄監督は、横浜映画学校１年の時の「演出」の授業をお持ちだった。監督作の大阪同郷のバタヤンこと川端康成原作「雪国」（６５）の演出とシナリオの違いを概説なさる半期授業だった。
　カントを大阪下町人にしたように超まじめな私は、「雪国」の原作をばらばらにして、シナリオの該当箇所にファイルアップして、授業開始を待ち、１度目は出たところ、その２ヶ月ほど前、日比谷東劇でテオ・アンゲロプロスの２３０分の「旅芸人の記録」（７５）を１日に２回見た※１記録をもっていた私に、いや授業の中で、「あんなの、パンフ見なけりゃわからんもんなど映画なんかじゃない！※２」と言われ……。
　去年、１年先輩の三池崇史監督のウィキペディアを読んだら、大庭監督の意見とくいちがいがあり、映画学校の授業に出なくなった、みたいなこと書いてあるのに、驚き……。私は、（城戸賞受賞することになる）２時間シナリオ提出したあとの二学期からはほとんど出ている。
　が、たしかに「君の名は」（５３）の監督とは学校パンフで知ってはいたし、ラジオドラマ放送の時は女湯がカラになったというような都市伝説も知ってはいたけれど、で、バタヤンの小説も好きくなかったし、（また、６０にもなって、判り始めてきたなどと書くと、この変態じじいがと誤解もされるのもシャクだしで。南無）
　大庭先生の授業だけでなく、１学期の授業は、夏休み終わりまで提出の２時間用映画のシナリオ作りに執心した。３時起きの新聞奨学生で、とくに午前中はヤタラ眠いし、学割きかない「映画スクール」だったので、定期など買ったことなく、交通費の削減にもなったりで。
　が、ある時、大庭監督の方から「キン君、なぜ授業でないの」と、不意に声をかけていただき、私の名を知っているなどないともおもっていて、まるで返事にならないアワアワとなったが……当時はビデオというものが、大金持ちか電器メーカーの家（注１）にしかない時代で、大庭監督の映画を見るわけにも行かず、だから授業で「雪国」をといういまだ内容つかめない小説にも興味わかずで……。
　だが、映画学校を卒業して２０年はたったあと、その２６の時の、第一回監督作品川島雄三「還ってきた男」（４６）の陣中見舞いを大阪から大船撮影所にしたとき、なんと３ショットの写真を撮られていたことを知って。あに図らんや、覆水盆に返らず、こぼれたミルクもグラスにもどらず……（哀）オー！マイゴッド！
　とくに、織田作之助の声一つこの世に残っておらず（ラジオに２．３度出たはずなのに、NHKも消失💢）
　その笑い方一つだけ大庭監督にきかせていただいても恩人となるはずだったのに。ネットなき時代が、にくい。

※１　当時は、まだ入れ替え制ではなかった。
※２　私も、総論は反対だけど、３時間ものなぜ原爆作った化粧品会社の名前みたいな者の映画見る必要など、ない、映画じゃない、などと、その各論には今なら、鋭意、同意賛成できる。
注１なぜ、「家」にあるか――ほぼＶＨＳシステムだったのに、ソニーのみが、他システムのベーターだったので、その（駆逐するためなどの？弱点）モニタリング仕事もあったりで。
Incidentally, Hideo Oba—director of *Your Name* (1953)—taught a "Directing" course during my first year at the Yokohama Film School. It was a semester-long class in which he outlined the differences between the original novel *Snow Country*—written by his fellow Osaka native, Yasunari Kawabata—and the screenplay for his own film adaptation (1965).
Being an incredibly earnest student—much like the "Osaka working-class" version of Kant—I took the original *Snow Country* apart, organized the text to correspond with specific sections of the screenplay, and waited for the class to begin. I attended the first session, but when I mentioned that I had watched Theo Angelopoulos’s 230-minute *The Travelling Players* (1975) twice in a single day at the Hibiya Togeki theater about two months prior, Oba-sensei remarked, "A film that you can't understand without reading the program pamphlet isn't a film at all!"
Last year, I was surprised to read on the Wikipedia page for director Takashi Miike—who was one year ahead of me—that he stopped attending classes at the film school because he disagreed with Oba-sensei’s views. As for me, I attended almost every class from the second semester onward, after I had submitted a two-hour screenplay (which would go on to win the Kido Award).
To be fair, I was aware from the school brochure that he was the director of *Your Name* (1953), and I knew the urban legend that public bathhouses for women would empty out whenever the radio drama version was broadcast. Furthermore, I wasn't particularly fond of Kawabata’s novel. (And I’d rather not write about how I’ve only begun to truly grasp it now that I’m sixty—lest I be misunderstood as some sort of "perverted old geezer." *Namu*.)
Beyond just Oba-sensei’s course, I spent the entire first semester—right up until the end of summer vacation—devoted to crafting a two-hour feature film screenplay. As a "newspaper scholarship student" who had to wake up at 3:00 a.m., I was perpetually sleepy—especially in the mornings. Since my "film school" didn't offer student discounts, I never bothered buying a commuter pass; not having one actually helped me save on travel costs.
One day, Director Oba suddenly asked me, "Kin-kun, why aren't you attending class?" I hadn't imagined he even knew my name, so I was completely flustered and couldn't manage a coherent response. Back then, video players were luxuries found only in the homes of the ultra-wealthy or families connected to electronics manufacturers—so watching Director Oba’s films was out of the question. Furthermore, I had no interest in the novel *Snow Country* (Yukiguni), which was the subject of our class—I couldn't even grasp what it was about.
Twenty years after graduating from film school, I visited the Ofuna Studios from Osaka to offer some encouragement during the production of *The Man Who Returned* (1946)—the directorial debut of Yuzo Kawashima. To my surprise, I discovered that a three-person photograph had been taken of us back when I was twenty-six. Alas—what’s done is done; spilled milk cannot be put back into the glass... (Sigh) Oh, my God!
It’s particularly painful because not a single recording of Sakunosuke Oda’s voice remains in this world—even though he appeared on the radio a few times, those recordings have been lost by NHK! 💢
If only I could have asked Director Oba about the way Oda laughed—that alone would have made him a true benefactor to me. I despise the fact that we lived in an era before the internet.

*Note 1: At the time, theaters did not yet use a "rotating" (fixed-session) screening system.*
*Note 2: While I might disagree with the general premise, I can now wholeheartedly agree with the specific arguments—such as the idea that there’s no need to sit through a three-hour film by someone whose name sounds like a cosmetics company that manufactured atomic bombs, or that such a work doesn't even qualify as "cinema" in the first place.* Note 1: Why was it in the "home"? Given that the VHS system was the dominant standard, Sony’s use of a different system—Betamax—meant that there was a need to monitor it (perhaps to facilitate its elimination from the market?).

text:
The Echoes of Her Wings
She walks the world as light walks water—
soft, and yet the surface never stays the same.
A beautiful woman, and in her wake the air
remembers. A glance becomes a turning.
A quiet word, offered like bread,
finds its way into another’s hunger
years later, in a room she will never enter.
This is the oldest truth the mystics knew:
nothing small remains small.
The butterfly does not measure the wind
it starts; it simply opens.
So does she.
Her kindness is not loud enough
to be called a sermon,
yet somewhere a life changes course
because she once stayed when leaving
would have been easier.
The echoes are not always sound.
Sometimes they are the courage
another person finds at midnight
and does not know why.
Sometimes they are the gentleness
passed from hand to hand
like a cup that has never been empty.
We think we leave footprints.
What we leave are currents.
What we leave is the way the light
leans differently after we have passed.
She does not see most of what she moves.
That is the mercy of it.
The soul is not asked to carry
every consequence it sets in motion—
only to move with care,
only to open its wings
and trust the larger air.
Long after her name has softened
into the stories people tell
when they are trying to explain
why they became kinder,
the ripples will still be traveling.
Somewhere a stranger will choose mercy
instead of the harder thing,
and will not know
that the choice began
with a beautiful woman
who once looked at the world
as if it were already holy
and then, without announcement,
made it so.

text:
When we had our first 10 customers at Octolens, I knew every name and what they were building. At 100, I kept up pretty well, but some were off my radar. Now at many hundreds, the blind spot keeps growing.

Keeping this blind spot as small as possible is my #1 priority.

Here are the things I do every day to work against it and keep customer obsession alive, because I'm convinced it's what got us this far:

1. I still own customer support

A few weeks ago, I allowed myself to add AI replies based on our docs for nights and weekends, but otherwise it's all me, and I check every AI response in the morning.

We also now offer a Slack Connect channel to every customer who converts, and it's GREAT for feedback.

2. I use Octolens for social listening daily

At this point, we get a good amount of brand mentions ourselves to learn from. On top of that, we track competitors and industry terms to get even more feedback. People are definitely honest on Reddit and X.

Everything is routed either to a Slack channel for me to see or to a scheduled task in Claude for analysis.

3. I look at every qualified trial signup

Completed onboarding → Slack notification → I qualify → goes to Attio for an outreach flow where I help and offer a call

4. I watch PostHog recordings and run through onboarding every week

We're constantly tuning onboarding, and I try to put myself in the shoes of someone who's never seen Octolens or a social listening tool before.

Sometimes I can hardly watch a session recording, because UX I thought was great turns out to be really unintuitive.

5. I offer 15-minute demos in the app and in every email

There's literally a little picture of me in the app and a button to book a demo call that anyone can use.

__

What's tricky is that the blind spot is a result of things going well. The more you grow and the more customers you have, the further you naturally drift from the people using your product.

It doesn't fix itself, so you need to actively work against it.

text:
Regional Real Estate Roundup

There's never a dull moment in South Baldwin County commercial real estate! From a million-dollar land sale in Orange Beach to new businesses, exciting development plans and major investments in infrastructure, there's plenty happening across our coastal communities.

Here's a look at what's making headlines in Orange Beach, Gulf Shores, Foley and Robertsdale!

Orange Beach: A Million-Dollar Deal on Canal Road!

Let's start with a big one! The west lot of Pelican Plaza, located next to Melanie Martin Interiors and Blalock Seafood on Canal Road, recently sold for an impressive $1 million!

The 1.32-acre parcel brought approximately $757,576 per acre, or $17.39 per square foot, believed to be the highest price per acre achieved for a land sale along Canal Road.

Heather Harp of RE/MAX of Orange Beach represented the seller, while Tim Arant of RE/MAX Gulf Shores represented the buyer.

It's another exciting transaction highlighting the value of prime commercial property along one of Orange Beach's most established business corridors. Location continues to be a major factor in the commercial market, and this sale certainly gives property owners and investors something to talk about!

Baldwin County: A 180-Day Pause on Certain Rezoning Requests

One of the biggest topics in local development news is Baldwin County's recently approved 180-day rezoning moratorium.

On October 6, the Baldwin County Commission approved a temporary pause on certain rezoning applications within areas governed by county zoning regulations. The measure also includes restrictions involving new data center and renewable energy projects.

But don't mistake this for a halt to growth! The moratorium does not stop all construction or commercial development, and it does not automatically apply within the city limits of Orange Beach, Gulf Shores, Foley or Robertsdale.

The goal is to give county officials time to review land-use regulations and plan for future growth.

For commercial investors and developers, it's an important reminder that knowing a property's zoning and permitted uses before purchasing can make all the difference!

Gulf Shores: Coffee, Anyone? PJ's Coffee Plans New Location!

Coffee lovers may soon have another stop along the Foley Beach Express!

A new PJ's Coffee drive-through is proposed just south of Coastal Gateway Boulevard, near the new Gulf Shores High School.

The Baldwin County Planning and Zoning Commission approved the site plan October 1 for the approximately 511-square-foot building on 0.87 acre.  It's another example of how commercial businesses are looking toward growing traffic corridors and expanding neighborhoods for their next locations.

Gulf Shores: Waterway Village Keeps Getting Better!

There's more activity happening around Gulf Shores' Waterway Village!

The city continues working toward public plaza improvements surrounding the pedestrian bridge over the Intracoastal Waterway.

At the October 19 City Council meeting, officials were scheduled to consider construction agreements and approximately $1.2 million in additional funding for the improvements.

The vision is to create better pedestrian connections and welcoming public spaces that could bring additional activity to nearby restaurants, shops and businesses.

Waterway Village is definitely an area to keep an eye on as these improvements take shape!

Foley: What's Next for Magnolia Walk?

Foley continues to grow, and Magnolia Walk is another development worth watching!

Located near OWA along the Foley Beach Express and Miflin Road, the approximately 99-acre mixed-use development is part of the ongoing investment activity in one of South Baldwin County's growing commercial corridors.

At its October 19 meeting, the Foley City Council was scheduled to consider additional economic development and project financing agreements involving SCP/BPG Magnolia Holdings LLC.

While specific tenants and future businesses have not yet been confirmed, the project represents another opportunity for commercial investment and development in Foley.

With so much activity along the Foley Beach Express, it'll be interesting to see what takes shape next!

Foley: Making Room for More Industry!

Foley isn't just growing in retail and restaurants. Industrial development is getting attention, too!

On October 5, city officials considered rezoning approximately 121 acres near North Juniper Street and Foley Beach Express for the proposed North Foley Industrial Park. The planned industrial park could create opportunities for manufacturing, warehousing, distribution and other businesses looking to establish a presence in Baldwin County.

More industrial development means the potential for additional jobs, business investment and economic activity throughout the area.

Robertsdale: More Commercial Development on the Horizon!

Robertsdale is getting in on the action, too! A construction project listing published in early October outlines plans for a 5,479-square-foot retail building and a 3,936-square-foot service station/car wash facility.

The proposed project carries an estimated construction value of approximately $1.52 million and was listed in the post-bid stage. Its exact location and construction timeline have not yet been confirmed.

With its central location and convenient access to Highway 59 and Highway 90, Robertsdale continues to offer opportunities for businesses serving Baldwin County's growing population.

Until Next Time

Whether you welcome the ongoing development or view it with a cautious eye, staying informed is essential as our coastal communities evolve. The goal of the Real Estate Roundup is to bring you clear, objective updates on the projects, decisions, and changes shaping South Baldwin County—ensuring you always know what is happening in your own backyard.

About the Author

Heather Harp is a commercial and residential real estate professional with RE/MAX of Orange Beach, specializing in commercial investment properties, land sales, development opportunities and business transactions throughout Baldwin County and the Gulf Coast.

text:
The Evolution of the Guitar Volume Pedal, 1930s–2026

The volume pedal allows amplified guitar control without interrupting playing. Hawaiian and lap-steel musicians used foot controls before World War II to soften attacks and extend perceived sustain. Unlike tremolo, a volume pedal provides continuous amplitude control.

By 1948, Rowe Industries of Toledo, Ohio, offered the DeArmond Model 600. Its rocking metal treadle mechanically operated a potentiometer, changing output without external power. The foot effectively replaced the hand on the guitar’s volume knob.

During the 1950s, Paul Bigsby developed a combined volume-and-tone pedal. Forward-and-back movement controlled volume, while side-to-side movement adjusted tone. Fender introduced its own volume pedal in 1954, followed by the dual-axis Volume Tone in 1958. Both remained in Fender’s catalog until 1984.

Pedal-steel players demanded smooth, repeatable control. Goodrich Sound, founded by Philip Goodrich in 1965, specialized in this market. Its cord-operated models, including the later H-120 family, translated treadle movement into potentiometer rotation. The founding date is not the Model 120’s introduction date.

The next important change was optical control. Tel-Ray/Morley pedals became prominent during the 1970s, using a lamp, movable shutter and photosensitive component instead of a mechanically driven audio potentiometer. DeArmond also produced an optical model, the 1630. Optical designs reduced potentiometer contact wear, although their light sources and electronic components still required maintenance.

Ernie Ball introduced its volume pedal in 1977. An aluminum treadle and cord-driven potentiometer offered a straightforward, unpowered design. Later versions accommodated different source impedances, and its familiar mechanism became a pedalboard standard.

As rack processors and electronic instruments proliferated, BOSS expanded the category with FV-series pedals. The later FV-500H and FV-500L offered high-impedance mono and low-impedance stereo versions, respectively, plus expression outputs.

Active and contactless designs further changed the technology. Hilton developed infrared-controlled pedals; Telonics introduced digitally selectable response tapers while preserving an analog audio path. Lehle’s Mono Volume, introduced in 2015, used a Hall-effect magnetic sensor to control an analog voltage-controlled amplifier, avoiding a conventional audio potentiometer. The smaller Mono Volume S followed in 2022, adding USB MIDI capabilities.

Ernie Ball’s 2020 VPJR Tuner integrated active volume control and a digital tuning display. By 2026, pedals could attenuate audio directly or transmit expression and MIDI control data to another device.

Passive pedals can load high-impedance pickups and change treble response, particularly with long cables. Buffered or active designs help manage impedance, while expression pedals generally carry control voltages rather than guitar audio.

Placement remains fundamental. Before overdrive, a volume pedal changes the signal driving distortion; afterward, it changes the distorted signal’s level. Positioned before delay or reverb, it can silence new notes while existing repeats and reverberation decay. The underlying purpose has not changed: precise musical dynamics underfoot.
